html:
Operation Solomon was a secret Israeli airlift that flew 14,325 Ethiopian Jews from Addis Ababa to Israel on 24 and 25 May 1991, in about 36 hours.

The Beta Israel, the Jews of Ethiopia, had lived for centuries in the northern highlands, cut off from other Jewish communities. In the 1980s famine and civil war pushed many to flee. Operation Moses in 1984 and 1985 had already brought thousands out through camps in Sudan.

By May 1991 rebel armies were closing in on the capital and the regime of Mengistu Haile Mariam was collapsing; Mengistu himself fled the country days before. Thousands of Jews had gathered in Addis Ababa, and Israel feared they would be caught in the fighting. It reached a deal with the failing government, reportedly paying it to let them go, and the rebels agreed not to interfere.

Thirty five aircraft flew nonstop, among them Israeli Air Force C-130s and El Al Boeing 747s stripped of their seats. One 747 carried over a thousand people, a record for a single flight. The newcomers then faced a hard settling in, with poverty and prejudice.
sum: Operation Solomon was a secret Israeli airlift that flew 14,325 Ethiopian Jews from Addis Ababa to Israel on 24 and 25 May 1991, in about 36 hours.
